Ashanti Region

Ashanti

Come for Kumasi’s energy, then look closer at the craft, history and market knowledge that give the region its depth.

Kejetia, one of West Africa's largest markets · Photo: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada

Capital

Kumasi

Go for

Kumasi, markets, kente and Asante history

Good to know

The region is the historic heartland of Asante culture.

Worth the trip.

Places in this region people keep coming back to. Not a ranking — a starting point.

  • Manhyia Palace Museum

    The Asantehene's former palace, now a museum of Asante history.

    Official site ↗Visit Ghana guide ↗Wikipedia ↗

  • Kejetia Market

    One of the largest markets in West Africa.

    Wikipedia ↗

  • The Great Hall, KNUST

    A landmark of Ghanaian modernist architecture.

    Official site ↗Wikipedia ↗

  • Lake Bosomtwe

    A meteorite crater lake ringed by villages.

    Visit Ghana guide ↗Wikipedia ↗

  • Bonwire

    The kente weaving village.

    Wikipedia ↗

  • Ntonso

    Adinkra cloth, stamped by hand.

    Wikipedia ↗

Festivals in
Ashanti.

Festivals and cultural events kept here, in calendar order. Many dates move from year to year, so each festival’s page has what we know about when.

  • Early Aug

    Yaa Asantewaa Festival

    Ejisu honours Nana Yaa Asantewaa, the queen mother who led the 1900 war against the British.

    Usually early AugustEjisu

  • Every 6 weeks

    Akwasidae

    The Asantehene sits in state at Manhyia and receives chiefs and visitors, every six weeks.

    Every six weeks, on a SundayManhyia Palace, Kumasi
